stem:
The diagram shows a mirror fixed at a sharp bend on a road near Yash’s colony so drivers can see traffic around the corner.

Why is a convex mirror chosen for this use?

options.text: It forms erect, smaller images and gives a wider field of view than a plane mirror
It forms a magnified image so distant vehicles look larger than life
Any curved mirror works the same, so concave would serve equally well here
It is chosen only because the glass looks shiny, not because of image size or field of view

teacher.key_rationale: Convex mirrors give erect diminished images and a larger view area, which suits side-view and road-safety mirrors. Magnification, treating concave as equivalent, or choosing by shine alone miss the reason.
teacher.figure_note: Convex mirror at a road bend with wide incoming view rays.
